intro: Exmouth, on the tip of the North West Cape, is one of the few places in Australia where the continental shelf runs within a short run of the boat ramp. Charter boats leave Exmouth Marina on the Gulf side or Tantabiddi on the Ningaloo side and can be trolling for blue, black and striped marlin and sailfish soon after clearing the reef.

Inside Ningaloo Reef and around the reef edges, charters chase Spanish mackerel, giant trevally, coral trout and spangled emperor, while deeper drops hold red emperor, ruby snapper and goldband snapper. Exmouth Gulf adds sheltered water and, each spring, sailfish packs feeding on bait. Most operators run private day charters for up to six to eight anglers, with some live-aboards to remote islands including the Montebellos.
exmouth.season: Fishing runs year round. Local operators say billfish can be caught in every month, with different species peaking at different times, and Exmouth Gulf sailfish sight-casting is sold only in October and November. Reef fishing for red emperor and coral trout is available all year, weather permitting.

items: Blue, black and striped marlin, sailfish, yellowfin tuna, wahoo and mahi mahi, often within minutes of the reef
Reef edges and bommies for coral trout, spangled emperor, Spanish mackerel and giant trevally
Sheltered water for queenfish, trevally, longtail tuna and the October-November sailfish run
Red emperor, rankin cod and mackerel around the islands at the top of the Gulf; live-aboards run on to the Montebellos

p: Gameboats work from Exmouth Marina (Madaffari Drive) or launch at Tantabiddi boat ramp on the Ningaloo side, which is closest to the shelf. Several operators collect guests from town accommodation.
items: Ningaloo side, closest to the shelf

p: Check the Ningaloo Marine Park zoning before fishing; licensed charters work within it. Paying guests on a licensed fishing tour do not need their own Recreational Fishing from Boat Licence. Many billfish are tagged and released; reef fish are usually filleted for you. Check the current DPIRD Gascoyne bag and size limits, which changed for demersal species from 1 June 2026.

faq: Can you catch marlin from a day charter in Exmouth?

Yes. Because the continental shelf is unusually close to the coast, blue, black and striped marlin and sailfish are targeted on full-day charters from Tantabiddi and Exmouth Marina. Private gameboat days typically run around eight to nine hours.
When is sailfish season in Exmouth Gulf?
Operators sell dedicated Exmouth Gulf sailfish days in October and November, when large numbers of sailfish follow bait schools into the gulf.

intro: Broome sits on Roebuck Bay at the south-west corner of the Kimberley, and its charters split into two styles. Small open boats work the mangrove creeks and bay, including Dampier Creek and Crab Creek, for barramundi, threadfin salmon, mangrove jack and tripletail, timed around big tides. Larger vessels head 10 to 40 nautical miles offshore for red emperor, coral trout, golden snapper and trevally, trolling for Spanish mackerel and tuna along the way.

Dedicated gameboats also chase sailfish and black marlin off Broome, and a few live-aboards run to the Rowley Shoals. Unlike the West Coast, boat-based demersal fishing remains open in the North West.
broome.season: The dry season, roughly April to October, brings calm mornings and is peak time for offshore reef trips; operators run daily then. Creek barramundi and threadfin fishing is often best around the build-up and wet season from October to March, when some reef boats only run on demand. Tides drive creek trip times all year.

items: Dampier Creek, Crab Creek and Black Ledge for barramundi, threadfin, mangrove jack and mud crabs
10-20nm on half days and 20-40nm on full days for red emperor, coral trout and golden snapper
Sailfish and black marlin on dedicated gameboats
Remote atolls about 168nm west, reached on multi-day trips

p: Creek boats usually meet at Entrance Point boat ramp or a Roebuck Bay landing. The larger reef boat transfers guests by tender from Gantheaume Beach or Entrance Point, and most operators include accommodation pickup.

Broome's tidal range can exceed nine metres, so trip times shift daily and wading the flats is dangerous on a rising tide. Saltwater crocodiles live in the creeks and mangroves. Licensed charter clients do not need a boat fishing licence. Barramundi and demersal species have bag and size limits under the North Coast rules, which changed from 1 June 2026; check the current DPIRD rules.

faq: Should I book a creek trip or a reef trip in Broome?

Creek trips use small boats for barramundi, threadfin and mangrove jack and are timed to the tide, usually for up to three or four anglers. Reef trips go offshore on bigger boats for red emperor, coral trout and mackerel and suit families and groups.
How big are Broome's tides?
Broome's tidal range can exceed nine metres, which is why charters plan creek trips around the tide and depart times change from day to day.

intro: The Kimberley is Australia's barramundi frontier: a huge, sparsely populated coast of mangrove creeks, rock bars and gorge-lined rivers, most of it reachable only by boat. Fishing here means either a live-aboard mothership working the coast from Broome or Wyndham, or a land-based guide out of Kununurra on the Ord River system.

Live-aboards fish creeks and rivers such as the Glenelg and bays like Talbot, Doubtful and Secure Bay for barramundi, threadfin, mangrove jack and fingermark, with trevally, queenfish and reef fish around the islands. In the east, Lake Kununurra and the Lower Ord hold barramundi year round thanks to regulated river flows, and guides take visitors to remote waterholes on Aboriginal Country.
kimberley.season: Kimberley coast live-aboards run in the dry season, roughly late February or April through to October. Some mothership fishing-only trips are timed for October, when big female barramundi gather before the wet. Around Kununurra the dam-regulated Ord gives a year-round river fishery. Check road conditions with the Kununurra Visitor Centre.

items: Glenelg River, Talbot Bay, Dugong Bay, Secure Bay and Doubtful Bay on live-aboards from Broome
Lake Kununurra and the Ord River
Over one million barramundi released into Lake Kununurra since 2013
Estuary fishing for barramundi, threadfin, fingermark, mangrove jack and mulloway near Wyndham
Remote East Kimberley rivers and waterholes on guided 4WD trips
Dry season live-aboard window on the Kimberley coast
Some live-aboards switch to the Rowley Shoals and Scott Reef for bluewater species
Lake Kununurra and the Lower Ord, conditions permitting

p: Saltwater crocodiles live in almost every Kimberley waterway that holds barramundi: stand back from the edge and never clean fish at the water's edge. Big tides drive fishing times along the coast. Some live-aboards warn that Traditional Owner visitor pass fees may be added to trip costs. Check the current DPIRD North Coast barramundi rules before keeping fish.

faq: How long are Kimberley fishing live-aboards?
Most run about a week or more. For example, Broome-based live-aboards publish nine-day itineraries for up to six anglers, with all meals, accommodation and tackle included.
Can you fish for barramundi around Kununurra?
Yes. The Ord River below the dams and Lake Kununurra fish year round, and the lake has been restocked with more than a million barramundi since 2013. Local guides run day and overnight trips.

intro: Perth's offshore fishing has changed. Since 16 December 2025, charter fishing for demersal scalefish such as WA dhufish, pink snapper and baldchin groper has been closed in the Perth metropolitan area, and boat-based recreational demersal fishing across the West Coast bioregion stays closed until spring 2027.

What remains is some of the best summer game fishing in southern Australia. Out past Rottnest Island, the deep water of the Perth trench (Rottnest Trench) draws marlin, mahi mahi, tuna and wahoo, and private gameboats run there from Hillarys Boat Harbour. Licensed West Coast charters can also offer rock lobster fishing.
perth.season: Charter game fishing in the Perth trench runs from about November to March for marlin, mahi mahi, tuna and wahoo. Boat-based demersal fishing for dhufish and snapper is closed until spring 2027, and charter demersal fishing in the metro area is closed until then too.

items: Deep water west of Rottnest for marlin, mahi mahi, tuna and wahoo
Inshore waters; check Rottnest Island Reserve rules

p: Most Perth fishing charters leave from Hillarys Boat Harbour in the northern suburbs; Fremantle is the other main base.

Under the 2025 reforms, charter demersal fishing is closed in the metro area from 16 December 2025, while charters with demersal tags can keep fishing for demersals elsewhere in the West Coast bioregion under a reduced 25-tonne catch limit. Pink snapper in Cockburn and Warnbro Sounds have a 1 August to 31 January spawning closure. Paying charter guests do not need a boat licence. Check the current DPIRD rules before you go.

faq: Can you still catch dhufish on a Perth fishing charter?

Not in the metro area. Charter fishing for demersal scalefish, including dhufish and pink snapper, has been closed in the Perth metropolitan area since 16 December 2025, and boat-based recreational demersal fishing in the West Coast bioregion is closed until spring 2027.
When is marlin season off Perth?
Perth game fishing charters target the trench off Rottnest from about November to March for marlin, mahi mahi, tuna and wahoo. Marlin are usually tagged and released.

intro: The Houtman Abrolhos Islands lie about 60 kilometres west of Geraldton: 122 islands in three groups (Wallabi, Easter and Pelsaert) stretching across 100 kilometres of ocean, protected as a national park. The warm Leeuwin Current lets southern fish like WA dhufish, pink snapper and samsonfish share reefs with coral trout and spangled emperor.

Most visiting anglers fish the islands on three- to six-day live-aboards out of Geraldton, trolling for Spanish mackerel and tuna, working reef edges for baldchin groper and coral trout, and pulling rock lobster pots. Day trips to the islands and near-coast charters also run from Geraldton when weather allows.
geraldton.season: Abrolhos live-aboards typically run from late summer into winter, roughly late February to June, with operators setting their own windows. The Abrolhos baldchin groper spawning closure runs 1 October to 31 December. Demersal fishing is now limited: only charters holding West Coast demersal tags can keep demersal fish, so ask your operator before booking.

items: Southern group; Wreck Point for trolling, western reefs for dhufish, baldchin and coral trout
Northern group, home of the Batavia wreck sites
Half and full-day trips when the islands are out of reach

p: Live-aboards and day boats leave from Geraldton's Batavia Coast Marina or the Fishermans Wharf area.

The Abrolhos is in the West Coast bioregion, where boat-based recreational demersal fishing is closed until spring 2027. Licensed charters with demersal tags can still fish for demersals outside the Perth metro area under a reduced 25-tonne annual limit. The islands have their own possession and bag limits; check the current DPIRD rules. Camping on the islands is not permitted.

faq: Can I keep dhufish on an Abrolhos charter in 2026?

Only with an operator that holds West Coast demersal tags. Charter demersal fishing outside the Perth metro area continues under a tag system with a 25-tonne annual catch limit, and some Abrolhos operators say they still offer dhufish. Confirm with your operator.
How far are the Abrolhos Islands from Geraldton?
About 60 kilometres west, usually around three hours by charter boat to the southern Pelsaert Group.

intro: Dampier and Karratha are the gateway to the Dampier Archipelago's 42 islands and, further offshore, the Montebello Islands, a remote marine park just north of Barrow Island. The Pilbara coast offers tropical reef fishing for red emperor, coral trout, rankin cod and spangled emperor, plus pelagic action on Spanish mackerel, giant trevally, tuna and sailfish.

Most visiting anglers fish the Montebellos on five- or six-day live-aboards, flying into Karratha and departing from Dampier, or from Onslow further south. Demersal fishing remains open in the North West under the 2026 bag and size limits.
dampier.season: Montebello live-aboards run in the dry season, roughly July to November depending on the operator, with Spanish mackerel, giant trevally, sailfish and reef fish the main targets. Operators do not publish summer trips.

items: Remote coral islands north of Barrow Island; GTs, coral trout, red emperor, Spanish mackerel
42 islands close to Dampier, crossed on the way out
Reef fishing on the run to and from the Montebellos

p: The Montebello Islands marine park has zones with special rules, so check before fishing. New North Coast demersal bag and size limits applied from 1 June 2026; charters set their own per-guest fillet limits within those rules. Paying charter guests do not need a boat fishing licence.

faq: How do you get to a Montebello Islands fishing trip?
Most anglers fly from Perth to Karratha and board in Dampier; some live-aboards depart from Onslow instead. Trips usually last five or six days.
How much fish can you take home from the Montebellos?
That depends on the current DPIRD North Coast rules and the operator's own limits. One Dampier live-aboard sets a maximum of 15kg of demersal and 5kg of pelagic fillets per guest per trip.

intro: Western Australia's charter fishing runs from the temperate south-west to the tropical Kimberley. In the north, Broome, Exmouth, Dampier and the Kimberley offer barramundi, threadfin, billfish and tropical reef fish, and boat-based demersal fishing remains open under new 2026 limits.

In the south, the West Coast bioregion from Kalbarri to Augusta is in a demersal recovery period: boat-based recreational fishing for dhufish, pink snapper and baldchin is closed until spring 2027, and Perth metro charters cannot target demersals. Game fishing off Perth and live-aboards with demersal tags at the Abrolhos continue.
western-australia.season: Go north in the dry season (April to October) for Kimberley barramundi live-aboards, Broome reef trips and Montebello trips. Exmouth fishes year round, with Gulf sailfish in October and November. Perth's marlin and mahi mahi run from about November to March, and Abrolhos live-aboards from late summer into winter.

items: Barramundi, threadfin and reef fish; dry-season live-aboards and creek guides
Marlin and sailfish close to shore, plus Ningaloo reef fishing
Montebello Islands live-aboards for GTs, red emperor and mackerel
Live-aboards mixing southern and tropical species
Summer game fishing in the Perth trench

p: DPIRD says paying guests on licensed charter fishing tours do not need a Recreational Fishing from Boat Licence, but they must follow recreational rules such as bag and size limits. If you fish from your own powered boat anywhere in WA, you need a boat licence. Demersal rules changed in 2025 and 2026; check the current DPIRD rules for the bioregion you are fishing.

In the Kimberley and Pilbara, saltwater crocodiles live in rivers, creeks and estuaries, and tides of eight to nine metres or more change conditions quickly. Choose licensed operators who know local tides and marine park zones.

faq: Do I need a fishing licence on a charter in Western Australia?

No boat licence is needed for paying guests on a licensed fishing tour. DPIRD states that paying guests on charter fishing tours are not required to hold a Recreational Fishing from Boat Licence. Recreational bag and size limits still apply.
Is dhufish fishing open in WA?

Not by boat in the West Coast bioregion (Kalbarri to Augusta), where boat-based recreational demersal fishing is closed until spring 2027. Some licensed charters outside the Perth metro area can still fish for demersals under a tag system.
